target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (F : ArithmeticTheory) [F.RE] [𝗜𝚺₁ ⪯ F], Def3 F →
    ∃ _ : Theory.RE (F ∪ {Def7 F}),
      Def3 (F ∪ {Def7 F}).theory ∧ Def7 F ∈ (F ∪ {Def7 F}).theory ∧ Def7 F ∉ F.theory ∧
        Def7 (F ∪ {Def7 F}) ∉ (F ∪ {Def7 F}).theory
translation: Target is a proposition stating that for every set F of arithmetic sentences (an arithmetic theory, not required to be closed under deduction) satisfying three hypotheses—(i) F is recursively enumerable, (ii) every theorem of IΣ₁ is a theorem of F (IΣ₁ ⪯ F), and (iii) every sentence in F is true in the standard model ℕ (Def3 F)—if we let c(F) denote the consistency sentence Def7 F = F.craig.consistent.val (that is, ¬Prov_{F.craig}(⌜⊥⌝), built from the standard provability predicate of Craig's Δ₁ presentation of F) and let F' = F ∪ {c(F)}, then: (1) F' is recursively enumerable (which also supplies the recursive-enumerability hypothesis needed to form c(F') = Def7 F' = F'.craig.consistent.val), (2) every sentence derivable from F' (i.e., every element of F'.theory) is true in the standard model ℕ, (3) c(F) is derivable from F' (c(F) ∈ F'.theory), (4) c(F) is not derivable from F (c(F) ∉ F.theory), and (5) c(F'), the consistency sentence ¬Prov_{F'.craig}(⌜⊥⌝) built from Craig's Δ₁ presentation of F', is not derivable from F' (c(F') ∉ F'.theory). No separate consistency or Δ₁-presentation hypothesis on F is assumed, and both consistency sentences are specifically those obtained via Craig's trick applied to F and to F ∪ {c(F)}.

divergences.description: The consequent fixes the second machine to the specific single-axiom extension F ∪ {Def7 F} rather than quantifying over an arbitrary enlarged machine F' that proves Def7 F. In Lucas's passage, the mechanist may construct any more adequate second machine and that machine still has its own Gödelian formula; however, because Target is universally quantified over all sound r.e. theories extending IΣ₁, applying Target to any sound r.e. enlargement F' of F still implies Def7 F' ∉ F'.theory.

Both unprovable formulas are consistency sentences built via Craig's trick (F.craig.consistent.val and (F ∪ {Def7 F}).craig.consistent.val) rather than diagonal Gödel sentences constructed by Gödel's procedure as described in the passage. The author's claim notes this substitution for the first machine, and over IΣ₁ the consistency sentence and Gödel sentence are provably equivalent, though the passage specifically invokes Gödel's procedure for the second machine's formula as well.

Target formalizes machines as recursively enumerable axiom sets in first-order arithmetic extending IΣ₁ and assumes full truth in the standard model ℕ (Def3 F, yielding Def3 (F ∪ {Def7 F}).theory). These exact formal assumptions—especially full arithmetical soundness rather than a weaker consistency/Σ₁-soundness condition—are idealizations not explicitly stated in the excerpt.

For the second machine's formula Def7 (F ∪ {Def7 F}), Target explicitly states only its unprovability (Def7 (F ∪ {Def7 F}) ∉ (F ∪ {Def7 F}).theory) and omits an explicit conjunct asserting that it is true in ℕ (Def2 (Def7 (F ∪ {Def7 F}))), though its truth follows from Def3 (F ∪ {Def7 F}).theory and the properties of the standard consistency predicate (or by re-applying Target to F ∪ {Def7 F}).

judgement.summary: Target faithfully captures the core logical content of Lucas's second-machine passage for the stated claim: for any sound r.e. arithmetic system extending IΣ₁, adjoining its consistency sentence yields a sound r.e. enlarged system that proves the previously unprovable sentence yet cannot prove its own consistency sentence. The only divergences are minor formalization choices, notably fixing the second machine in the consequent to F ∪ {Def7 F}, using Craig-presented consistency sentences instead of diagonal Gödel sentences, assuming full arithmetical soundness and IΣ₁ ⪯ F, and leaving the truth of the second consistency sentence implicit.
